title: Market Structure
lessons/trend-u3-l1/title: Highs and Lows: HH, HL, LH, LL
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/0/body: To read market structure, compare each **High** and **Low** with the one before. An uptrend means **HH** (higher high) and **HL** (higher low): on this chart, every low is above the previous low and every high is above the previous high.
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/1/body: A downtrend is the reverse: **LH** (lower high) and **LL** (lower low). If the highs and lows sit at roughly the same level, the market is **ranging**.
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/2/prompt: What label goes on the point marked "?"
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/2/explanation: This point is a high, and it went above the previous high. So it's an HH, and the bullish structure is still intact.
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/3/prompt: In this downtrend, tap the most recent lower high (LH).
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/3/explanation: The last high before the final drop formed below the previous high. That's the LH. As long as price stays below it, the bearish structure is intact.
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/4/statement: In a downtrend, price makes lower highs (LH) and lower lows (LL).
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/4/explanation: That's the definition of a downtrend. Every time price bounces, it falls short of the previous high and then makes a new lower low.
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/5/pairs/0/mean: A high above the previous high
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/5/pairs/1/mean: A low above the previous low
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/5/pairs/2/mean: A high below the previous high
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/5/pairs/3/mean: A low below the previous low
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/6/body: A **swing high** is a candle whose high is above the candles on both sides, after which price really turned (a swing low is the reverse). Don't count tiny wiggles; look for clear highs and lows on **the timeframe you trade**.
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/6/tip: If you have to squint hard to find the trend, the market probably doesn't have a clear one.
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/7/prompt: What about this one? What label goes on the "?" point?
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/7/explanation: This high didn't reach the previous high, so it's an LH. More LHs and LLs mean the downtrend is still in place.
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/8/sentence: In a downtrend, every new high is labeled ___ and every new low is labeled ___.
lessons/trend-u3-l1/steps/8/explanation: A downtrend means both the highs and the lows keep getting lower: Lower High and Lower Low.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/0/body: In an uptrend, when price **closes above the last high**, that's a **Break of Structure (BOS)**: the trend is **continuing**. In a downtrend, a BOS means a close below the last low.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/1/body: The first warning that an uptrend may reverse is when price closes **below the last higher low (HL)**. This first break against the trend is called a **Change of Character (CHoCH)**: buyers couldn't defend their low anymore.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/2/prompt: The blue line marks the last higher low (HL). Tap the first candle that closed below it.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/2/explanation: This is the first candle whose body closed below the last HL: the first serious warning for the uptrend (CHoCH). Every candle before it stayed above that low.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/3/prompt: What story do the labels on this chart tell?
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/3/options/0/la: The trend flipped from up to down
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/3/options/2/la: The market ranged the whole time
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/3/options/3/la: The trend flipped from down to up
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/3/explanation: First we had HLs and HHs (bullish). Then price broke the higher low and made an LL, the next high stayed lower (LH), and the new low broke too. LH and LL structure means the trend has turned down.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/4/statement: In an uptrend, a close above the previous high (BOS) usually signals the trend is continuing.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/4/explanation: A BOS with the trend means buyers still have the strength to make a new high. A break against the trend (CHoCH) is the warning of change.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/5/prompt: USD/JPY is in an uptrend. Put the line on the last higher low (HL): the level where a close below it gives a bearish CHoCH.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/5/explanation: The last HL is the low that formed before the break of the 150.30 high: 149.95. As long as price stays above it the structure is bullish, and a close below it is the first sign of a trend change (CHoCH). The 149.54 low is an older HL.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/6/body: A CHoCH on its own is just a **warning**. Many traders wait for price to make a **lower high (LH)** and then break the new low too. That's when the bearish structure is **confirmed**.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/6/tip: CHoCHs happen a lot on lower timeframes. Check the higher-timeframe structure first.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/7/prompt: Put the usual steps of an uptrend turning into a downtrend in order.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/7/items/3: The low breaks and a lower low (LL) forms
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/7/explanation: The trend peaks with the last HH, the HL break is the first warning, the LH shows buyers are weak, and the LL confirms the bearish structure.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/8/prompt: After a downtrend, Ethereum broke its last lower high (CHoCH), made a higher low and is climbing again. What do you do?
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/8/explanation: The bearish structure broke with a CHoCH, and price made its first higher low (HL). That combo makes a new uptrend more likely. The logical stop loss is below that HL.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/9/prompt: EUR/USD is in an uptrend and the last HL is at 1.0820. Price is now at 1.0860. Which event counts as the first warning of a trend change?
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/9/options/2: A break above the previous high
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/9/options/3: Rising volume on the green candles
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/9/explanation: As long as price stays above the last HL, the bullish structure is intact. A close below 1.0820 means buyers failed to defend their low. That's the CHoCH.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/10/sentence: A break of the previous high in the direction of an uptrend is called a ___, and the first break against the trend is called a ___.
lessons/trend-u3-l2/steps/10/explanation: BOS means the trend continues, and CHoCH is the first sign the market's character is changing.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/title: Zones, Not Lines, and Round Numbers
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/0/title: Support is a zone, not a line
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/0/body: Price rarely comes back to the exact same number: once a bit lower, once a bit higher. So draw support and resistance as a **zone** that covers the **wicks and bodies** of past reactions.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/1/body: Round numbers like **1.1000**, **150.00**, **2400** or **60,000** matter to lots of traders, and plenty of buy orders, sell orders and stop losses cluster around them. That's why they often act as **psychological support and resistance**.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/2/prompt: What role does the shaded "?" zone play?
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/2/explanation: Price reached this area three times and got rejected every time. It isn't one exact number, but it's a clear range. That's a resistance zone.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/3/prompt: USD/JPY reached the round number 150.00. Tap the candle that bounced right off this level.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/3/explanation: This candle's long lower wick reached 150.00 and it closed higher. Buyers stepped in right at the round number, and price rose after it.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/4/statement: It's best to place your stop loss exactly on the round number or exactly at the edge of the zone.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/4/explanation: Price often pokes a little past a round number or a zone edge and then comes back. Put your stop a bit outside the zone so a simple wick doesn't take you out.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/5/prompt: Which number is likely the more important psychological level for EUR/USD?
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/5/explanation: 1.1000 is a perfectly round number, and lots of orders cluster around it. The other numbers mean nothing special to the market.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/6/body: The strongest levels are where several reasons meet: a **zone** that has reacted before, a **round number**, and **trend structure** (like an HL in an uptrend). This overlap is called **Confluence**.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/7/prompt: Gold is in an uptrend. It broke the 2400 resistance, came back to that zone and printed a strong green candle. What do you do?
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/7/explanation: The old resistance is now acting as support after the breakout, right on the round number 2400 and inside an uptrend. A continuation up is more likely. Stop loss just below the zone.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/8/prompt: You bought from the 2395 to 2405 support zone. Where do you put your stop loss?
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/8/options/0: A bit below 2395, outside the zone
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/8/options/2: At 2405, the top edge of the zone
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/8/options/3: No stop; the zone is strong
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/8/explanation: The whole zone is the reaction area. If price closes below the entire zone, the idea is broken. So the stop goes a little below 2395.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/9/sentence: Price rarely returns to the exact same number, so we draw support and resistance as a ___, not a thin ___.
lessons/trend-u3-l3/steps/9/explanation: A zone covers the wicks and bodies of past reactions and shows what the market really does better than a single line.
